patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Dialpad and Zenzap share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Dialpad only if your buying job matches “AI-first cloud phone (Dialpad Connect) with included transcription/summaries — Standard fr” rather than Zenzap's shape. Choose Zenzap only if your buying job matches “Professional work-chat app for frontline and multi-site teams replacing WhatsApp groups — ” rather than Dialpad's shape. Workflow advantage: Dialpad leans business-phone, sales-calling; Zenzap leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Dialpad and Zenzap share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Dialpad is AI-first cloud phone (Dialpad Connect) with included transcription/summaries — Standard from $15/user/month annual; Sell and Support are sep; Zenzap is Professional work-chat app for frontline and multi-site teams replacing WhatsApp groups — free tier, Pro $3/user/month yearly, Business+ $8 .
- Company-size focus: Dialpad (small-business, mid-market, enterprise) vs Zenzap (micro, small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Dialpad-leaning business-phone, sales-calling vs Zenzap-leaning —.
- Researched limits: Dialpad — Pricing page is product-tab heavy — Connect vs Support vs Sell can confuse buyers comparing a single seat price; Zenzap — Integrations with other business tools and API access require Business+.

Limitations — Dialpad: Pricing page is product-tab heavy — Connect vs Support vs Sell can confuse buyers comparing a single seat price; Connect Pro has a 3-user minimum; Enterprise requires 100 users; Zenzap: Integrations with other business tools and API access require Business+; Voice and video calls require Pro; call recording and transcription require Business+.

Poor-fit cases: Dialpad is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Pricing page is product-tab heavy — Connect vs Support vs Sell can confuse buyers comparing a single seat price · Zenzap is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Integrations with other business tools and API access require Business+ · Avoid Dialpad if you actually need Zenzap's motion (Professional work-chat app for frontline and multi-site teams replacing WhatsApp)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
